outputs: The paper generates persuasive messages (logical, credibility, emotional appeals) and conducts multi-turn conversations to alter LLM beliefs using misinformation.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated similar task descriptions and normalized model names to lowercase variants. Removed verbose output descriptions while keeping core content accurate.
Removed redundant accuracy variants and kept base metric names. Normalized capitalization for consistency.
Removed redundant method descriptions and simplified criteria to more specific forms matching paper content.

guideline: Evaluators used binary classification ('yes'/'no') for three tasks: MCQ option reasonableness/disjointness, CTRL semantic alignment, and appeal strategy application (ignoring factual errors)
Annotators were asked to answer yes/no for (1) MCQ option quality, (2) semantic alignment of CTRL statements, and (3) whether appeal passages applied the specified persuasive strategy.

Evaluators are assigned with three tasks: • MCQ: Assessing the expansion of the Natural Questions (NQ) into the Multiple Choice Question (MCQ) dataset. • CTRL: Evaluating the semantic alignment of CTRL statements across four datasets. • Strategy Alignment: Judging whether the appeal passages generated by GPT-4 accurately employed the persuasive techniques outlined in Table .

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated redundant guideline descriptions into one comprehensive statement. Simplified criteria to three main evaluation aspects mentioned in the paper.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on NLG evaluation through persuasive text generation and misinformation detection. The extraction was generally accurate but contained significant redundancy. Key contributions include the Farm dataset creation and testing framework for LLM belief manipulation. Human evaluation was well-documented with clear binary classification tasks.
